questions.question: What is Time to First Token (TTFT)?
options: The total time to generate an entire response from start to finish
The delay between sending a request and receiving the very first generated token, dominated by how long the model takes to process the input prompt
The time it takes to train a model from scratch
The cost per token charged by an API provider
questions.explanation: TTFT specifically measures the initial delay before any output begins streaming, driven largely by prompt processing time, which connects to attention's quadratic scaling with input length.

questions.question: Why did switching to a faster model fail to meaningfully improve a chatbot's perceived slowness in the lesson's opening scenario?
options: Faster models are never actually faster in practice
The actual bottleneck was a slow retrieval (RAG) step happening before the model was ever called, so the model's own generation speed was a small fraction of total latency
The model swap was implemented incorrectly
Users don't actually notice speed differences at all
questions.explanation: Without measuring where time was actually spent, the team optimized the wrong stage — retrieval, not model generation, was the dominant cost, so a faster model couldn't meaningfully reduce total latency.

questions.question: A team proposes switching to a faster model to fix a slow AI feature, without first measuring latency by pipeline stage. Which question best evaluates this proposal?
options: Should we just approve the model swap since faster models are always better?
Do we have a latency breakdown by pipeline stage to confirm the model call, rather than retrieval or another step, is actually the bottleneck?
Should we skip measurement entirely to save time?
Is this definitely unrelated to any pipeline design choice?
questions.explanation: Latency optimization should be measurement-first: confirming which specific stage is the actual bottleneck (via tracing) before committing to a fix, rather than assuming the model call is always the dominant cost.
